identity.title: The global stability of the Kaluza–Klein spacetime

findings.title: Hyperboloidal integration and the scaling-ray initial term leave the available bootstrap domains
findings.decisive_evidence: An exterior target t=15,r²=195 has fixed hyperboloid s²=30; at allowed dyadic time9 its radius²=51 is below the exterior threshold63. For the strictly interior target t=49,s=10, the s0=21/10 ray starts at time1029/100, beyond the truncated H_s0 maximum441/200; entry is lambda=49/5. A smooth zero-average bump near that start has positive Y(s0) and zero truncated initial energy. Reference21 p28 explicitly extends estimates to whole hyperboloids before its analogous ray argument.
findings.alternative: An extension to whole hyperboloids with proven exterior energy/pointwise bounds, or rays starting at max(s0,2t/s) with adequate boundary traces, may repair the argument. Neither is established here for this Einstein system.
findings.impact: The sharpened exterior LT estimate and nonzero-mode pointwise bootstrap enter the main energy closure; this is a proof-domain gap, not a counterexample to Theorem1.2.
findings.repair_status: Substantive boundary/extension estimates required; not completed by this review.

findings.title: The characteristic estimate in Lemma4.13 is false as printed and its boundary and mass hypotheses need revision
findings.decisive_evidence: Take Minkowski g, pi=0, and smooth u(x)=rho(r)/r, rho=0 near0 and1 for r>=1. Its smooth forcing is supported in r<1. At t10,r11,s5 the characteristic is r(tau)=tau+1>=3. The RHS of(4.72) is0, including the boundary derivative of ru, but its LHS is10/121. Also the backwards interior ray from(10,6) hits r=t/2 at(8,4), excluded by t<=8/3. At r=t the printed |pi_LL| bound is0, whereas the mass tail is -2M/t plus a faster-decaying remainder.
findings.alternative: Retain the u term when converting Lbar(ru) to r Lbar u, define a domain below the terminal hyperboloid with its full relevant boundary, and prove a characteristic statement compatible with the mass tail. Replacing |t-r| by1+|t-r| alone does not verify all geometry.
findings.impact: Invalidates a stated auxiliary lemma used for good-component decay and the ensuing weak-null estimates. It does not disprove the nonlinear Einstein stability theorem.
findings.repair_status: Exact counterexample established; full replacement lemma and application not supplied.

findings.title: Separate fixed-mass smallness from uniform positivity of the separating-surface flux
findings.decisive_evidence: Near a large point on the separator let g00=-1-M/r+a, grr=1-M/r, a=epsilon(1+t+r)^(-3/2). For dW=(1,-x/(t-1),0), tangential derivatives vanish and e_curved=1/2[1/(1+r²)+(M/r)(1+r²/(1+r²))-a]. At epsilon1/100,M1/100000000,r100000000 this is -1.61776692644986479e-15. The residual H_LL+2M/r equals a and obeys the stated delta1/2 decay locally; smooth localization preserves the bound.
findings.alternative: For each fixed positive M, sufficiently small epsilon depending on M may restore coercivity. Additional Einstein/gauge/constraint structure might also prevent the auxiliary witness. Neither uniform implication is assumed.
findings.impact: A quantitative parameter-dependence and application check is needed before treating the boundary flux bound as uniform over M tending to0.
findings.repair_status: Explicit auxiliary metric calculation complete; nonlinear applicability intentionally unresolved.

findings.title: Use consistent exterior slices and truncated hyperboloids
findings.decisive_evidence: The energy integrates r>=t-1 but Sigma_e uses r>=sqrt(t²-2t). A smooth bump near(4,2.9) has zero literal narrow-domain energy but nonzero wide-slice gradient norm. The p16 t>=r+1 truncation gives t<=(s²+1)/2, while the separator truncation used elsewhere gives t<=s²/2.
findings.alternative: Define energy integrals over the actual D_e slices and use H_s={t²-r²=s²} intersect D_i throughout, retaining the corresponding boundary terms.
findings.impact: Local definitions must be corrected; this does not by itself establish failure of the corrected energy estimates. Consequential path gaps are separately P1.
findings.repair_status: Exact mismatch and natural correction supplied; all nonlinear estimates not reconstructed after correction.

findings.title: Missing factor two in the null-to-hyperboloidal coefficient identity
findings.decisive_evidence: For arbitrary radial contravariant tensor components A,B,C, the exact formula has 2*pi_L_Lbar. With pi00=1 and all other components0, the left side minus the printed right side is exactly1. Symbolic general verification of the corrected identity gives0.
findings.alternative: Replace the mixed term by2*pi_L_Lbar and propagate constants.
findings.impact: Schematic absolute-value estimates tolerate the correction; no additional asymptotic loss is forced.

findings.title: Correct the semi-hyperboloidal drift and associated equation signs
findings.decisive_evidence: The exact drift in -Box is(3/t-r²/t³)partial_t, not the printed plus sign. Testing u=t leaves2r²/t³; the printed Q has residual2s²r²/t³ partial_t u. For Box u+A*u_tt+R=G the correct isolated equation is((s/t)^2-A)u_tt=-L+R-G. The mass source has negative sign in(1.8) and is subsequently defined with the opposite sign.
findings.alternative: Use the exact drift and consistent source signs, regenerate Q from P=S²+2S+3/4, and repeat the displayed algebra before taking absolute values.
findings.impact: The affected terms have already available derivative size and coefficient smallness; these are local identity corrections, independent of P1's domain gap.
findings.repair_status: Corrected operator and Q residuals verified symbolically; no claim that every later printed formula has been rewritten.

findings.title: Restore the variable-mass derivative in the oscillator energy and the original cutoff argument
source_locations: pp59–62 Proposition4.21 energy calculation and b,R,A definitions
findings.decisive_evidence: For b*omega''-c*omega_yy-d*omega'_y=R with coefficients independent of y, E'=b'||omega'||²+c'||omega_y||²+2<R,omega'>. The displayed equality omits c'. With omega=lambda*cos(y),b1,c1+alpha*lambda, the defect is pi*alpha*lambda². The same section writes chi(t/r) where the actual mass tail uses chi(r/t).
findings.alternative: Restore c' and use chi(r/t) consistently. A_tx already budgets the c' derivative; the mixed y term integrates to0.
findings.impact: Local repairs preserve the available Gronwall structure within its valid domain; the unresolved domain issue remains P1.
findings.repair_status: Exact energy calculation and cutoff discrepancy verified.

findings.title: State the uniform time-flux estimate actually needed in the exterior bootstrap
findings.decisive_evidence: Cumulative flux F(t)=t^(2sigma)-2^(2sigma) gives normalized l(t)=2sigma/t. It is L1 on every finite interval but its total norm grows as2sigma log(T/2). The available uniform conclusion is dyadic L1 control; then integral_R^2R t^-a sqrt(l) is O(R^(1/2-a)) and summation is finite for a>1/2.
findings.alternative: Use the dyadic estimate explicitly, choose sigma and rho with margins such as sigma<1/6 and2sigma<rho<kappa/2 where required, and handle a last partial dyadic interval with a justified full-window argument.
findings.impact: A uniform-in-lifespan justification is missing in the written inference. Weighted dyadic control provides the required analytic mechanism; path-domain issues are still P1.
findings.repair_status: Scalar inference and replacement summability proved; not a full reconstruction of Proposition3.3.

findings.title: The zero-mode source cutoff does not have the stated exterior support
findings.decisive_evidence: An admissible decreasing cutoff chi equal1 up to1/2 and0 after1 may have chi(3/4)=1/2. At(t,r)=(10,7),1-chi((r+1/2)/t)=1/2 although t-r=3>1/2. Thus its complementary forcing is not confined to the asserted exterior cone.
findings.alternative: Use eta(t-r), zero for t-r<=1/2 and one for t-r>=1. Its first forcing is supported where Lemma4.29 applies and its complement lies in D_e; use t2 initial data consistently.
findings.impact: The local source partition must be repaired before using the quoted scalar wave estimates; the available overlap allows a direct corrected split.
findings.repair_status: Support counterexample and corrected partition provided.

The target (10,11) lies in the exterior branch of D_s. The function is smooth at the origin, independent of y and time, and satisfies the displayed differential equation and coefficient hypotheses.

Every stated lateral boundary radius is >=1, so Lbar(ru)=0 there and the angular, forcing and coefficient terms on the ray are zero. Nevertheless t|Lbar u|=10/121. Algebraically r Lbar u=Lbar(ru)+u. Separately, the admissible interior target (10,6), s=6 reaches the inner boundary at (8,4), excluded by the printed t<=8/3 condition. finding_checks.assumptions_and_quantifiers: The cumulative flux has nonnegative density and F(t)<=C*epsilonÂ²*t^(2sigma), with sigma>0. Distinguish a bound on each finite interval from a constant uniform in its upper endpoint.

Generally the cumulative bound gives integral_R^(2R)l<=2^(2sigma), and Cauchy-Schwarz gives the weighted bound C_a*R^(1/2-a). The dyadic sum converges for a>1/2.

Sufficient margins include sigma<1/6 and, where needed, 2sigma<rho<kappa/2. An arbitrarily short final partial interval still needs a justified full-window or endpoint treatment.

The replacement summability argument is available without additional assumptions, so this bookkeeping correction remains Minor; the independent path failure remains P1.
